headline: Application for $2,403,510.02 in passenger facility fees to fund airport security checkpoint work approved.
summary: These passenger facility fees are $4.50 per plane ticket, not airport or city money. The project also includes bathrooms next to the checkpoint that must be brought up to ADA compliance, and a skylight replacement. If the application is approved, two council orders would go to the full council. Also recommended for the full council: $20,000 in arts grants and a three-year Irving Oil contract extension; a parcel sale failed 2-2.
decisions: Approved the airport's application for $2,403,510.02 in passenger facility fees, 5-0.
Approved accepting and appropriating the $2,403,510.02 if received from that application, 5-0.
Approved the change to the GE Vernova lease, 5-0.
Recommended approval of five arts grants totaling $20,000 to the full council, 5-0.
Recommended a three-year contract extension with Irving Oil at the airport, 4-0.
Rescinded the motion to move forward on the TIF and CEA for the Milford Street extension; staff will get more information first.
Failed 2-2 to recommend selling two parcels back to A&L Webster, LLC.
discussion: Community and economic development overview: The director described four divisions and said staff plan videos on some projects, to be posted on the city website, so councilors can view them on their own time.

Airport checkpoint funding: The airport director said the FAA asked that the bathroom and skylight work be placed in a separate funding application. The work was part of the project that went out to bid.

Cultural grant tax forms: A member asked that applicants again submit 990 forms to show they are current, since a 501(c) status alone does not show a group is active; staff said the application could be changed to ask for it.

Cultural grant economic effects: A member asked how much visitor spending the $20,000 in grants brings to the city. Staff said a Downtown Bangor study from several years ago looked at other visitor spending, but they did not have the figure.

Milford Street TIF cost: A member asked how much the outside help would cost, since the city would spend money even if the application is not approved. Staff said they had not yet talked to them and could get an estimate.
